method: Independent qualitative pixel comparison; no taste score or formal approval

coverage.round: first versions only; originals remain unchanged
coverage.views: For every01–20: complete member/public desktop/phone overview; individual native member desktop/phone top, middle and bottom; public desktop/phone top-middle-bottom checkpoint composites. Final20-theme desktop and phone contact sheets also seen.
limits: Complete long pages were fit-to-view overviews, not text legibility evidence at every vertical position.
Native member three-point crops and public checkpoint panels sample top/middle/bottom; not every table row or intervening pixel was enlarged.
Public desktop checkpoint panels are half native scale.
Default captured member/public states only; no expanded menus, search results, full roster disclosures, text zoom, keyboard focus, hover or alternate AI states tested by this visual critic.
No rework captures inspected in this first-version report.
No author DESIGN/allocation narratives or other critics’ reports read before or during judgments.
This covers only assigned63 pairs; root must reconcile the complete upper triangle.

pairs.reason: Both are dark neon sports worlds. 01 uses condensed white headings, lime/lavender scores and a faint full court; 04 uses cyan/pink pixel headings, offset arcade frames, a game-led opening and a two-column team register. Those differences persist below the hero. Bounded separation: keep 04’s arcade frames and pixel typography in lower sections; do not turn either body into the other’s flat row system.
01 stays navy with sharp lime/lavender condensed rows; 07 alternates green, off-white and gold programme bands with slab lettering and boxed paired club cards.
01 is a condensed neon night-court page with purple panels; 10 is a blue monochrome drawing sheet, with monospaced type, continuous graph paper, lettered rail and diagram navigation.
01 uses dark court lines and small data portraits; 13 builds a light lavender/orange collector world around tilted portrait cards, rounded display type and a full lower-page card binder.

Both use tall condensed sports headings over a dark, ruled data page. 01 has a navy/lime/lavender court plan and repeated colored roster anchor bars; 16 uses a black/gold photo overlay, film-like angled opening edges and a narrow numbered body rail with gray portrait chips. Bounded separation: carry 16’s cinematic framing into its dated-edition and archive treatment so its restrained body retains a stronger identity.
01 is nocturnal navy with luminous condensed scoring and purple panels; 19 is a light concrete-gray industrial register with red numbered dividers, boxed black indices and fluorescent total block.
02 uses huge wide black/white editorial slabs and grayscale portraits; 04 uses dark purple, pixel headings, cyan/pink rules and offset arcade outlines throughout.
02’s alternating pure black/white numbered sheets and heavy sans differ from 07’s green/gold club programme, slab headings and two-column boxed register.
02 is high-contrast black/white print with oversized wide headlines; 10 is an all-blue technical drawing with small mono labels, fine grid lines and lettered sections.
02 uses grayscale rule-bound editorial sections and wide heavy sans; 13 uses lavender/orange bands, playful rounded type, tilted cards and a portrait binder.
02 alternates white and black sections around broad editorial typography; 16 remains nearly black, uses narrow condensed headings, gold accents and an arena overlay with numbered side rail.

Both are square, print-like grayscale sports registers with numbered sections. 02’s huge wide display type, alternating pure black/white sheets and large left indices differ from 19’s constant concrete-gray field, narrow condensed headings, red rules and black index boxes. Bounded separation: preserve the alternating slab composition in 02 and the continuous industrial ledger in 19; a palette swap alone would collapse that distinction.

The opening in both is an arena photo darkened behind a scoreboard, followed by restrained near-black ruled data. 05 uses wide futuristic display numerals and cyan/chrome highlights, keeps top values as a separate large section and places standings beside rosters. 16 uses tall condensed type, gold film edges, a combined seat/value block and numbered left rail; standings come after rosters. Bounded rework recommendation: strengthen 16’s cinema language in one editorial and one lower section; retain its distinct rail and avoid 05’s chrome display treatment.

Bounded separation: keep 06’s street-paper edge and handwriting and 14’s serif/light editorial interruption; do not flatten both into the same dark brown row page.

Both use geometric sans type, rounded color fields and portraits against shaped backgrounds. 15 has saturated royal blue/yellow/coral, overlapping offset score shapes, bold wide headings and strong outline/shadow accents. 20 uses pastel mint/lavender/coral, quiet thin rules, pill controls and arch portraits; its score stays inside a soft white card. Bounded separation: keep 15’s overlap and saturated rhythm and 20’s quiet inset treatment through archives and team lists.

Both use tall condensed headings, restrained arena imagery and rule-separated sports data. 16 is black/gold with a full photo-overlay opening and left numbered rail; 19 is light concrete-gray with red vertical/horizontal dividers, boxed roster numbers and a separate anchor index after the register. Bounded separation: preserve those body structures and strengthen 16’s film framing beyond the hero so a future gray/gold palette change cannot erase the distinction.

18 maintains a compact early-web sports portal with navy title bars, orange keylines, beveled square controls, white table cells and dense side modules. 20 uses airy pastel fields, pills, arch portraits and soft rounded sections.
